clue.text: Late boss to tidy 5

definitions.note: 5 is the flower; to deadhead a plant is to tidy it by snipping off its spent blooms

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died
a head is the boss of a school or department

explanation.surface: Someone tells their boss, who is running late, to go and tidy up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 cross-reference is the flower, so the definition is a gardening chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners remove withered blooms to keep a plant neat and encourage more flowering.

clue.text: Summary of what stomach does

definitions.meaning: a condensed account or abstract of a longer text
the stomach breaks food down, the verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a condensed summary and the verb for breaking down food in the gut.

clue.text: A catch in the neighbourhood

parts.note: a catch is a type of round, a song sung in overlapping parts

explanation.surface: A fish caught somewhere locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests fishing, but it is the musical sense: a catch is a round, sung like Frere Jacques.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nearby or about the place is the adverbial sense of the word.

clue.text: Housekeeper for Norfolk?

parts.note: the house part gives HO, the usual abbreviation for house
the keeper part gives WARD, a guard or keeper, as in warden

explanation.surface: Someone asks who keeps house for the Norfolk family.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard is the family name of the Dukes of Norfolk, so 'Norfolk?' defines by example; Norfolk is an English county and its dukedom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Howards hold the dukedom of Norfolk, so the surname is the ducal family's name.

clue.text: Frequently unwarranted intruder presenting a job for the right workman?

parts.note: a post is a job or position
the work part gives OP, short for opus, a work
the man part gives HE, the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A job for a proper tradesman is offered to an unwelcome intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workman' splits into its two halves. The intruder is the stray punctuation mark that turns up where it is not wanted, as in a greengrocer's "apple's".
explanation.definitionFit: The mark is often misused, sneaking uninvited into plurals where no possessive is wanted.

clue.text: See 18
Realistic precursor of a dome of many-coloured glass

definitions.text: precursor of a dome of many-coloured glass
definitions.meaning: in Shelley's Adonais the words before 'a dome of many-coloured glass' are '...'

explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means true to nature, and the two words open Shelley's famous line about the dome.

clue.text: Musical sound in court to end dispersal

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: dispersal scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: In a law court, music is played to bring a dispute to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the verb of romance, not the law; 'dispersal' rearranges TO END into DNOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodnote is a natural, untrained musical call, like birdsong.

clue.text: Part of car or tram or distributor

indicators.note: a distributor deals things out, so it scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of where some component might be found: in a car, a tram, or a distributor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributor' looks like part of the list but rearranges OR TRAM OR; the component does indeed sit inside a car's distributor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating contact in the ignition distributor is a component of a car engine.

clue.text: Applause for bowler at place to race

definitions.meaning: in bowls, players praise a good shot by calling out about the wood (the bowl)
a racecourse in West Sussex, England

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is praise shouted in lawn bowls and also the name of a famous English racecourse.

clue.text: A supplier of milk at sea?

parts.note: a milk float is the electric van that delivers milk in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is a milkman out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is the small British milk-delivery van. The question mark marks 'at sea' as being afloat literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea means floating on the water rather than aground.

clue.text: Miss one's train, the last having gone, unhappily

indicators.note: unhappily here signals these letters being put into disorder

parts.note: taken as its letters, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the final letter of the word train is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone misses their train, which has unfortunately already left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb but is the title for a young woman. 'The last having gone' cuts TRAIN to TRAI; 'unhappily' then rearranges ONES with TRAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Senorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Sense personified by 5 turning to gold

indicators.note: turning means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: 5 is the flower, read as something that flows: a river, here the Nile
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A flower changes colour to gold, as if given senses.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is crossword code for a river; turning the NILE gives ELIN. Elinor Dashwood embodies Sense in Austen's Sense and Sensibility.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jane Austen's novel the sensible elder sister Elinor stands for Sense against Marianne's Sensibility.

clue.text: Corrupter of mature queen by worker

parts.note: adult means grown up, mature
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a worker ant, the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A grown queen bee is corrupted by one of the workers in the hive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an insect colony, but each word just gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance added to spoil or debase something pure.

clue.text: Think about setting task for aquatic insect

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to ponder is to think

indicators.note: setting here means arranging the letters of task in another order

explanation.surface: Someone considers setting a job for a water bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' rearranges the word task, and 'about' wraps the thinking word round the result; 'setting task' reads at first as a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-legged bug skims across the surface of still water.

clue.text: M's extract from "A for 'orses" causes stress

definitions.meaning: in the comic Cockney alphabet that starts 'A for 'orses' (hay for horses), M is 'M for sis', said like the answer
importance or weight placed on something

explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney alphabet is a British music-hall joke where each letter is a punning phrase: 'A for 'orses' (hay for horses), 'M for sis'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying stress on something is giving it special prominence or importance.

clue.text: Picnic that puts the meat into sweetmeat

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a cake is a sweetmeat
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A picnic where the meat is baked inside a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetmeat' already holds the letters of meat, a red herring; 'puts the meat into' means one synonym goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is a seaside picnic where shellfish are cooked, typically on hot stones.

clue.text: Gather nuts and lichen initially from hell

parts.note: to gather in the sense of conclude is to infer

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A forager collects nuts and lichen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' suggests harvesting but means deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal describes something belonging to or coming from hell.

clue.text: What is 6? 2 says "fruit and veg"

indicators.note: 2 is the round, a song whose words are being quoted, so this is how it is sung

parts.note: a melon is fruit and a cauliflower is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A question about life, answered with a shopping list of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is LIFELIKE, so 'What is 6?' asks 'What is life?'; a round sung to Frere Jacques answers 'Life is but a melancholy flower', sung so it sounds like melon, cauliflower.
explanation.definitionFit: The round's lyric says life is but a melancholy flower, so the phrase answers the question.

clue.text: Stocking unit I say didn't happen?

definitions.meaning: a measure of the fineness of yarn used for hosiery
someone who says something did not happen is one who denies

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the unit of fineness for stocking yarn and, said differently, one who denies.

clue.text: Lord hasn't finished the poem involved in 6

indicators.note: the last letter of the poem's title is dropped

parts.note: Shelley's elegy for Keats, Adonais, contains the line quoted in 6

explanation.surface: God has not finished the poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't finished' cuts the final S from ADONAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonai is the Hebrew title meaning Lord, used for God.

clue.text: Swift agent keeping 5 upside down

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside down means the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: 5 is the flower, something that flows: a river, here the Dee

explanation.surface: A quick agent holds a flower upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'flower' is again a river; 'upside down' turns it to EED in this down entry, and 'keeping' holds it inside the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and speedy are synonyms for fast.

clue.text: Village drama society's production?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's tragedy, a stock play for amateur dramatic societies, with a hint of hammy acting

explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village, and Hamlet is the play an amateur dramatic society might put on.

clue.text: Return of food without tear from land of lucky finders

indicators.note: without means outside, so the first piece goes round the second
return means the word for food is read backwards

parts.note: pies are food
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: Food comes back without any tears from a fortunate country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here; 'Return of' turns the food into SEIP before it goes round the tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendip, an old name for Sri Lanka, gave Horace Walpole the word serendipity for lucky finds.

clue.text: Marks heard in Surrey

indicators.note: heard means the town's name is said aloud

parts.note: Staines is a town in the English county of Surrey

explanation.surface: Marks are heard of in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines (now Staines-upon-Thames) is a town in Surrey, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Stains are marks or blemishes left on a surface.

clue.text: Painter, one into movement of light

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dance is rhythmic movement
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter moves into the light.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is bright light shining out, and this word follows 'stains the white' in Shelley's line.

clue.text: Quoted poet sounds like Mary's garden

indicators.note: sounds like says the poet's name is said aloud

parts.note: Shelley is the poet quoted throughout this puzzle

explanation.surface: A much-quoted poet resembles a lady's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' has a garden of 'silver bells and cockle shells', so it is full of shells.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden decorated with cockle shells is literally covered in shells.

clue.text: English bird to Italian unknown for ever

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An English bird meets an Italian it will never know.
explanation.walkthrough: Eternity closes Shelley's line, 'Stains the white radiance of Eternity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, so for ever means for all eternity.
